meanings.definition: To restore friendship or peace between people after disagreement or conflict.
examples: The brothers reconciled after years of silence.
She hoped to reconcile with her old friend.
Community leaders worked to reconcile the two groups.
Their reconciliation brought relief to the whole family.

meanings.definition: To make different ideas, beliefs, or facts fit together or become compatible.
examples: He struggled to reconcile science and spirituality.
The historian tried reconciling conflicting records.
It is difficult to reconcile freedom with strict control.
She reconciled the two reports before presenting them.

meanings.definition: To accept something unpleasant or difficult and become at peace with it.
examples: He slowly reconciled himself to the loss.
She was trying to reconcile herself to change.
Many people reconcile with hardship through patience and support.
He never fully reconciled himself to leaving his hometown.

meanings.definition: To compare and check accounts, numbers, or records so that they match and are correct.
examples: The accountant reconciled the bank statements carefully.
They were reconciling financial records at the office.
Errors appeared while she reconciled the accounts.
Businesses reconcile expenses and income regularly.
